correctness.rationale: The theorem is about Hom(<x,y|x^p=y^q>, SL2(C)) reduced analytic topological space, not character quotient. Primary Liriano Lemmas 1–2 supply A≅SL2(C)≃S3 and g disjoint components Y_i≅Q×Q (Q≃S2) meeting A in two connected branches each, diagonal and antidiagonal Q. A finite closed semialgebraic cover admits compatible CW model, so integral Mayer–Vietoris applies. Antipodal U↦-U on Q induces degree -1 on H2(S2); the H2 intersection gluing per component is [[1,1],[1,-1]], of Smith (1,2), creating exactly one Z/2 in H2 per component, with no H2 kernel. H0 incidence has rank g, kernel Z^g and primitive image, giving H1=Z^g; H3 from A and H4 from Q×Q yield Z and Z^g. Higher homology vanishes. Independently calculated SNF of these blocks for coprime examples (2,3),(3,4),(5,7), not a substitute for the geometric component cover.

value.rationale: A natural and distinct topological space associated with classical torus knot groups has previously unaccounted integral 2-torsion. The exact all-(p,q) classification makes explicit a difference from rational invariants and singular-locus homology. This is a structural answer, not mere change of coefficient convention.

final_claim: For coprime p,q>1, the full reduced torus-knot SL2(C)-representation variety has H0=H3=Z, H1=H4=Z^g, H2=(Z/2)^g and no higher integral homology, where g=(p-1)(q-1)/2.
limitations: Only full reduced torus-knot SL2(C) representations, coprime p,q>1; excludes quotient, nonreduced structure, other knots/groups.
